inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 144.839m ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (Note 14) + 2.283m potential ordinary shares (Note 13 diluted WANOS 146.963m less basic 144.680m); held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). ~0.9m shares/yr are issued to the employee share trust for vesting rights; there is no buyback.

net_debt_bridge.note: Treatment (A): leases as debt, so lease liabilities (64.5m) are in the bridge and ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged inside capex_pct (~1.2% of revenue, = right-of-use depreciation 21.95m / lease principal 22.14m). The 55.2m current 'value chain' provision (Note 6, nil in FY25) is IEEPA Phase 1 tariff-refund cash received near year end and owed onward to value-chain partners within 12 months -- it is treated as debt-like, so the company's headline net cash of 104.4m (ex-lease) becomes net DEBT of 15.2m on this basis. Deferred tax, derivatives (0.7m) and other financial assets (3.6m) ignored.

inputs.sbc_source: Annual Report FY2026 Note 3(e) share-based payments expense 21,924 (thousands), cash-flow reconciliation 5(c); no separate equity-award tax withholding line (rights are satisfied by shares issued to the employee share trust, no net cash out), so the P&L expense is the full charge
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built: ACGB 10yr ~4.3% (Sept 2026, approximate) + equity risk premium 5.5% x beta ~1.05 (global consumer-discretionary hardware, ~49% Americas revenue, USD/tariff exposure) = ~10% cost of equity; net debt is ~0 on the model's bridge so WACC = CoE = 10.0%. Applied identically to all three scenarios: tariff/cyclical/competition risk is charged ONCE, in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate (owner-fcf.md s7f).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (dcf-methods routing: non-US consumer operating company -> owner-fcf.md + section 7). Breville designs and sells premium kitchen appliances (coffee ~ half of Global Product) across Americas/EMEA/APAC plus an ANZ Distribution segment; it is a straightforward operating company with real free cash flow. COMPONENT BUILD on a 10-year horizon: adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, post-AASB16; FY26 306.0m = 16.9%) -> less SBC -> less D&A (4.3% incl. ROU depreciation) -> cash tax 29-30% -> plus D&A -> less capex (PP&E + capitalised development + ~1.2% lease-asset renewal) -> less working capital at 25% of the revenue INCREASE (negative capture: inventory 465.8 + receivables 310.6 - payables 321.1 = 455.3m = 25% of revenue). The DB's EBITDA column (284.1m) is AFTER the SBC expense; the build starts from EBITDA + SBC so SBC is charged exactly once. LEASES: treatment (A) -- lease liabilities in net debt, renewal in capex, lease interest not in the flows. SBC: expensed at 1.2-1.3% of revenue (rising trend 0.7% FY22 -> 1.2% FY26), share count flat; Breville is a non-repurchaser, so the flat count is a modelling convention paid for by the SBC charge, not by buybacks. INTEREST INCOME (2.2m) stripped because cash (193m) is in the bridge. FY2026 BASE-YEAR CAUTION: OCF 220.7m includes ~55.2m of IEEPA tariff-refund cash provisioned for onward payment (treated as debt-like in the bridge, NOT left in the flows); reported FCF is very noisy (FY22 -84.8m, FY24 +240.5m) because inventory swings 50-75m/yr, so the projection is built from margins and a normalised WC drag rather than from last_fcf. TERMINAL: Gordon bound in all three scenarios (cap 18x owner FCF base/bull, 15x bear did not bind); base exit 14.7x owner FCF = ~11.9x terminal NOPAT, versus today's EV/adj-EBITDA of 14.2x and P/E of 30.8x -- the model assumes multiple CONTRACTION, and the gap to the market price is the market's growth/duration premium, not a hidden asset. Currency: statements and quote both AUD; no FX.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 15.9% vs revenue 5yr CAGR 8.8% (>30% divergence): equity growth is retained earnings at a ~40% payout plus rights-plan issuance, not a growth signal. Owner-FCF CAGRs are unusable -- FY2023 owner FCF was $6.1m (inventory build) and FY2022 was -$101m, so the 3yr figure is off a near-zero base and the 5yr figure (1.2%) reflects working-capital timing, not earnings power. Revenue 3yr CAGR (7.0%) selected.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC, interest income and lease-asset renewal) is far noisier than reported FCF and its 5yr CAGR (1.2%) is well below reported FCF's (6.9%): SBC rose 0.6m -> 21.9m over the decade (0.1% -> 1.2% of revenue) and lease renewal is ~22m/yr post-AASB16. FY2020-FY2026 owner FCF averaged 54.6m/yr (3.8% of revenue) against NPAT of 7-8%: the gap is working capital (~25% of revenue growth), capitalised development running ~1.7x its amortisation, and SBC. FY2026 owner FCF of 83.9m also carries ~55.2m of IEEPA tariff-refund cash booked as a value-chain provision (paid onward within 12 months); underlying FY2026 owner FCF is ~28.8m on a heavy inventory year.

base.narrative: Breville keeps compounding at roughly its FY23-26 pace: revenue +7% in FY27 (FY26 was +6.7% reported, +9.7% constant currency) decelerating to 3% by FY36 as the coffee category matures and the new direct markets (China, Korea, Middle East, Mexico) scale from a small base. Adjusted EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, post-AASB16) recovers from the tariff-depressed 16.9% toward 17.7% as the diversified 120V sourcing (85% of GP ex-China) removes cost volatility. Working capital stays a 25% drag on growth (inventory + receivables - payables = 25% of revenue), development capex runs ahead of amortisation, and SBC is held at 1.25% of revenue. Cash tax 29-30%.

bull.narrative: The last decade repeats. Revenue CAGR of ~12% (FY16-26 actual: 12.1%) for the first three years on China (7.1x the prior distributor in year one), Middle East (6.6x), Korea and the Best Buy store-in-store roll-out, then a normal deceleration. Premium coffee (Oracle Jet/Dual Boiler, Lelit, Baratza) keeps taking share, gross margin recovers above 37% once tariff pass-through is complete, and operating leverage lifts adjusted EBITDA to 19.5% by FY36. Better inventory turns cut the WC drag to 20% of revenue growth.

bear.narrative: The tariff regime and a soft US consumer bite. Americas (49% of revenue) stalls, tariff cost cannot be fully priced through, and Chinese espresso-machine competition compresses gross margin: revenue grows 2-3% p.a. and adjusted EBITDA slides to 14.7% (reported ~13.4%) by FY36. Working capital stays heavy at 30% of growth (inventory pre-build for peak seasons, longer supply chains from diversified manufacturing), SBC drifts up to 1.3% of revenue, and cash tax stays at 30%. No balance-sheet stress: the business remains profitable and net cash, so this is a de-rating, not a solvency, scenario.

entry_price.method: Price at which buying today, collecting the projected owner FCF for 10 years and exiting on a terminal value rebuilt AT the 15% hurdle (min(Gordon@15%, cap x FCF_10)) returns 15% IRR; per scenario, then probability-weighted.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_10)); 10% row = base IV, 15% row = base entry price.

sensitivity.note: Rows = WACC, columns = terminal growth; each cell rebuilds TV = max(0, min(Gordon, 18x FCF_10)).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 20/50/30 versus the house 15/50/35. Bear raised to 20% because the two bear axes -- US tariff policy (restructured four times in FY26 and still unresolved) and a US discretionary-spending slowdown (Americas 49% of revenue) -- are exogenous, correlated and unhedgeable. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs new-market scaling AND gross-margin recovery AND continued coffee-category share gain together. No going-concern or covenant risk (net cash ex-lease, $364m undrawn facilities), so the bear is a de-rating case, which is why it is not higher.
probability_weighted.band_note: Price A$29.40 sits 545% of the way from the house value (A$14.31) to the street value (A$17.08) -- i.e. far ABOVE both. SBC treatment is not what separates the model from the market (the house/street gap is only ~A$2.8/share); the market is paying for a lower discount rate and a longer growth runway than the house method grants.

current_multiples.note: EV is lease-inclusive and includes the 55.2m IEEPA provision as debt-like, matching the model bridge; EBITDA is post-AASB16, so the multiple is lease-consistent.

valuation_philosophy.summary: House owner-FCF DCF values Breville at A$14.31/share weighted (base A$13.64, bear A$8.05, bull A$19.60) against a A$29.40 price. The gap is not an error in the anchors: it is the difference between owner FCF (after SBC, after capitalised development, after a 25%-of-growth working-capital drag; 3.8% of revenue on average FY20-26) and the NPAT the market capitalises at ~31x. A buyer at today's price is underwriting roughly a 7-8% IRR on the base path (required-return table), or a decade of 12%+ growth with margin expansion (bull) at ~8%.
valuation_philosophy.what_would_change_it: Base-year drivers to refresh at the H1 FY27 print (Feb 2027): FY27 revenue growth vs the 7% assumed, gross margin trajectory post tariff pass-through, the unwind of the 55.2m value-chain provision, and inventory/WC after the FY27 peak season. Evidence that would move later years: sustained double-digit growth in the direct markets (bull weight up), or a US tariff settlement that restores >37% gross margin (base margin path up).

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
